stories.title: Remember that the disclaimer was accepted, so it is not shown again on reload
stories.description: Add src/app/storage.ts: a small safe wrapper around the browser's local storage (read, write, remove) that never throws — when storage is blocked or full it reports 'unavailable' instead (the history story F12-S6 uses it too). Keys carry the app name and a version, e.g. 'spineFluoroTrainer.disclaimerAccepted.v1'. When the learner accepts the disclaimer, save that; on the next load, skip the disclaimer if it was saved. If storage is unavailable, show the disclaimer on every load and keep working. Shared-file change, explicitly allowed for this story (owner decision 2026-11-11): two existing F2 screen tests reload the page and then call acceptDisclaimer() again, so change tests/fixtures/acceptDisclaimer.ts so that it accepts the disclaimer only when it is shown (it is decided while the page loads; check for the accept button) and otherwise returns straight away. Its name and how it is called stay the same; no test file changes. Unit tests use a fake storage object passed in (no browser page). Only the app zone edits src/app/main.ts.
acceptance: Unit test: the storage wrapper reads back what it wrote; with a storage object whose every call throws, reads give nothing, writes report 'unavailable', and nothing throws
Screen test (both set-ups): after accepting the disclaimer and reloading the page, the disclaimer is not shown and <html> has no data-disclaimer attribute
Screen test (both set-ups): in a fresh browser context (nothing saved) the disclaimer is shown

Screen test (both set-ups): with local storage blocked (an init script makes window.localStorage throw), the disclaimer is shown after accepting and reloading, and the app still works after accepting (a Shot is counted)
The existing screen tests still pass unchanged, including tests/e2e/render/invert.spec.ts and tests/e2e/render/noise.spec.ts, which reload the page
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/app/storage.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/app/rememberDisclaimer.spec.ts tests/e2e/app tests/e2e/render/invert.spec.ts tests/e2e/render/noise.spec.ts
stories.notes: Done 2026-11-11. src/app/storage.ts (createSafeStorage, storageKey, appStorage); main.ts skips the disclaimer when spineFluoroTrainer.disclaimerAccepted.v1 is "true"; acceptDisclaimer fixture returns straight away when no accept button is shown.

stories.title: Show a clear message instead of a blank screen when the browser has no WebGL2
stories.description: In src/app/main.ts, before mounting any zone, check that the browser can create a WebGL2 context (a plain check function in src/app/, given the canvas factory, so it can be unit-tested). If it cannot, show only the message "This browser can't run the simulator (WebGL2 needed)" (test id webgl2-missing) in a readable card, and mount nothing else (owner decision 2026-11-11: no disclaimer either, as there is nothing to use). The screen test stubs WebGL2 out with an init script that makes HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext return null for 'webgl2'. Only the app zone edits src/app/main.ts.
acceptance: Unit test: the check function returns false when the factory's getContext('webgl2') returns null or throws, and true when it returns an object
Screen test (both set-ups): with WebGL2 stubbed out, the page shows the exact message "This browser can't run the simulator (WebGL2 needed)" and none of the four main panels is visible
Screen test (both set-ups): with WebGL2 stubbed out, the page logs no uncaught errors (listen for 'pageerror')
Screen test (both set-ups): without the stub, the message is not shown
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/app/webgl2.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/app/webgl2.spec.ts
stories.notes: Done 2026-11-11. src/app/webgl2.ts (canUseWebgl2, showWebgl2Missing); main.ts checks before mounting any zone and shows only the message when WebGL2 is missing.

stories.title: Add the home screen with Free play, and a Home button on the simulator screen
stories.description: After the disclaimer, the app shows a home screen (test id home-screen) instead of going straight to the four panels. It offers four choices (F12.2): Practice, Exam, Quiz and Free play (test ids home-practice, home-exam, home-quiz, home-freeplay), plus History and About (home-history, home-about; their screens come in later stories, so for now they may be disabled). This story makes Free play work: it sets the store's mode to 'freeplay' and shows the simulator screen (the existing four-panel layout). The simulator screen gets a slim top bar with a Home button (test id home-button) that goes back to the home screen; the four panels must still fit without scrolling. Every zone is still mounted once at start-up, as now (tests/e2e/app/panels.spec.ts checks it); the home screen only hides and shows the simulator screen. Owner decision 2026-11-11: the app sets data-screen on <html> ('home', 'sim', and later 'quiz', 'procedures', 'about', 'history') so zones with page-wide shortcuts can ignore keys off the simulator screen, the same way they read data-disclaimer; teaching other zones to read it is a later shared change. Shared-file change, explicitly allowed for this story (owner decision 2026-11-11): change tests/fixtures/acceptDisclaimer.ts so that, after the disclaimer, it also chooses Free play (click on desktop, tap on tablet) when the home screen is shown, so every existing screen test still lands on the four panels; its name and how it is called stay the same, and no test file changes. Layout: on the tablet every button is at least 44×44 px and this story's screen tests check the app's own buttons. Only the app zone edits src/app/main.ts. Test change explicitly allowed for this story (owner decision 2026-11-11): tests/e2e/app/rememberDisclaimer.spec.ts (written in F12-S1) may be updated so that its tests choose Free play (home-freeplay; click on desktop, tap on tablet) before checking the panels or taking a Shot, or check the home screen instead of fluoro-panel after the reload. Its disclaimer checks stay as they are; no other existing test file changes.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): after clicking or tapping 'I understand' (directly, not through the fixture), the home screen shows the four choices Practice, Exam, Quiz and Free play, plus History and About, and the four main panels are not visible

Screen test (both set-ups; click on desktop, tap on tablet): Free play shows the four main panels, sets the store's mode to 'freeplay' (read through the dev server's store module) and sets data-screen to 'sim'

stories.title: Add the About page with the disclaimer, the dataset credits and the app version
stories.description: Add the About screen (test id about-screen), opened from the home screen's About button and closed with the Home button. It always shows the full disclaimer text (reuse the same text as src/app/disclaimer.ts, so the two never differ), the app version (import version from package.json — JSON imports type-check here; no change to package.json), and the dataset credits from the manifest. The manifest is the anatomy zone's file: read data/manifest.json yourself with fetch (relative to import.meta.env.BASE_URL; never import from src/anatomy/) and show, for each region, its source dataset name, licence and attribution text — owner decision 2026-11-11: the field names are those F1 writes (regions[].sourceDataset, regions[].licence, regions[].attribution). Treat the file as untrusted: check each field is text and put it on the page as text, never as HTML. When the manifest is missing, invalid or lists no regions (today's phantom-only build), show 'Images are computed from a synthetic test phantom; no patient data is used.' (test id about-no-dataset). Tests serve a made-up manifest with Playwright's page.route (fake dataset names and attribution only; nothing is added to public/data/).
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): the About page shows the disclaimer text, including 'For training only' and 'not for clinical use'
Screen test (both set-ups): it shows the version from package.json
Screen test (both set-ups): with a served test manifest of two regions, it shows each region's dataset name, licence and attribution text
Screen test (both set-ups): a served manifest whose attribution contains HTML tags shows the tags as plain text and adds no elements
Screen test (both set-ups): with no manifest (404) or one listing no regions, it shows the phantom-only text
Screen test (both set-ups): its buttons are at least 44×44 px; the Home button returns to the home screen
stories.notes: The manifest field names must match what F1 writes (F1-S17/F1-S18). Check them when F1 is reviewed; if they differ, this story's reader needs a small fix. stories.title: Add the history store: save attempt records in the browser, newest first
stories.description: Create src/app/history.ts with plain functions on top of the storage wrapper from F12-S1 (storage passed in, so unit tests need no browser page): add(record), list() newest first (by the record's date, then by order added), clear(), and available() (false when storage is blocked). Records are the shared AttemptRecord type (src/core/types.ts, read-only), kept under a versioned key such as 'spineFluoroTrainer.history.v1'. Whatever is read back from storage is untrusted: entries that are not valid attempt records are dropped, and a broken stored value gives an empty list instead of an error. Export a module-level history object for the app (as src/core/store.ts does for the store) so the history screen and the screen tests use the same instance. Plain TypeScript, no browser code in the logic.
acceptance: Unit test: added records come back newest first, both procedure and quiz records
Unit test: records survive a new history object made on the same storage (as after a reload)
Unit test: clear() empties the list
Unit test: a stored value that is not JSON, or that holds invalid entries, gives a list without them and no error
Unit test: with a storage that throws, available() is false, add() does not throw, and list() is empty
stories.notes: Done 2026-11-11. src/app/history.ts: createHistory(storage) with add/list/clear/available, toAttemptRecord(value) validator (returns a clean copy or null; F12-S11 can reuse it), module-level `history` on appStorage, key spineFluoroTrainer.history.v1.

stories.title: Add the History screen with Clear history and the storage-unavailable message
stories.description: Add the History screen (test id history-screen), opened from the home screen's History button, with the Home button back. It lists the finished attempts newest first (test id history-entry for each): date, mode, procedure (or 'Quiz'), total score, an 'Unsafe' mark when flagged, and shots and fluoro time when present; an empty history says so. 'Clear history' (test id history-clear) asks for confirmation in an in-page dialog (test ids history-clear-confirm and history-clear-cancel; not window.confirm, so it works the same with touch) and clears only after confirming. If browser storage is unavailable, the screen shows "History can't be saved in this browser" (test id history-unavailable) and the app keeps working. Procedures (F10) and the quiz (F11) do not exist yet, and saving the records they hand over is F12-S11, so tests add records through the dev server's src/app/history.ts module (the same trick as setPose), with made-up records only.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): three records added by the test are listed newest first, showing their scores and an 'Unsafe' mark on the flagged one
Screen test (both set-ups): after reloading the page, the same records are still listed
Screen test (both set-ups; click on desktop, tap on tablet): Clear history shows the confirmation; Cancel keeps the records; Confirm removes them, and they stay gone after a reload
Screen test (both set-ups): with local storage blocked (init script), the screen shows "History can't be saved in this browser", and Free play and a Shot still work
Screen test (both set-ups): every button on the screen and in the dialog is at least 44×44 px

stories.title: Lay out the simulator screen for landscape and stack the panels in portrait
stories.description: Make the simulator screen's layout meet F12.3: at 1280×800 and 1024×768 landscape (the two set-ups' own sizes) all four panels, with the top bar, are visible without scrolling the page; at 768×1024 portrait (the test sets this viewport, in both set-ups) the panels stack in one column with the fluoro panel first, then C-arm, needle and 3D view, and the page may scroll. Use CSS only (e.g. a media query on orientation or width); keep the fluoro image readable in portrait (its panel roughly as tall as it is wide). Other zones' panel contents are theirs; this story changes only the app zone's layout. Planning note: the PLAN says to re-check the layout once all panels exist (after F5–F10).
